meta.note: Per-market lessons from the editor's verdicts on machine candidates. Rendered into the judge prompt (prompts/quip-judge.md, {{LESSONS}}). Append a lesson per market each time he reviews a board; keep each one to what he did and why it beat the machine's pick.

lessons.text: Robot walks on Mars. Machine's top pick (scored 8.5): "we argued about budgets for sixty years and the toaster just went". He ignored it and built his line from a candidate scored 5: "Matt Damon in shambles" → shipped "Matt Damon didn't become the greatest botanist on the planet for this". A shared reference the reader already owns beats an original image every time.

Swallows beat the Carp. Top pick (8): "the Carp have not been relevant since my last haircut". He built from a candidate scored 6: "a bird beating a fish is nature at its most electric" → shipped it with a flat tag: "…that's Japanese baseball for you." The dumb literal observation delivered as awe wins, and a deadpan tag after the punchline is allowed when it adds attitude, not explanation.

Coquimbo Unido win. Top pick (8.5): "\"COQUIMBOOO\" — me, to my roommate, unprompted, on a Saturday". He built from a candidate scored 5: "like a Sun Belt team winning a bowl game nobody televised" → shipped "like a Sun Belt team winning an untelevised bowl game". The American-sports comparison is his home mode. Self-narrated performance ("me, to my roommate") reads as a bit being performed and he never picks it.

Leah becomes a Category 4. Candidate scored 9: "Tampa did something to deserve this and they know what it was" → he shipped "Tampa probably deserves this". Right idea, a third of the words. He passed over the other 9, "Leah sounds exactly like a girl who would do this to us".

Ohtani leads MLB in ERA. Top pick (8.5): "he takes the ERA title and apologizes to the runner-up in two languages". He took a candidate scored 8 verbatim: "Angels fans watching from a Denny's parking lot". Mean and specific beats gracious and clever.
Brex IPOs before Ramp. Nothing in sixteen candidates. He wrote "Begun, the corporate card war has". A famous syntax (Yoda) applied to the bet's own phrase, no explanation.

NASA on the Moon before 2028. He wrote "Cancel this and you could give every American $44 which is exactly this payout. coincidence? i think not." The bet's own numbers (the $ payout) are material, the voice is a conspiracy guy, and two sentences are fine when the second one is the joke.

US-Iran nuclear deal. Top pick (8): "my geopolitics guy in the group chat finally eats this week". He wrote "at this point I don't know how many deals we've had and I'm too embarrassed to ask". Weary first-person confession beats the "my group chat" device, which is a formula and scores 5 at best.
Drew Allar starts: he shipped the machine pick untouched, "he throws for 94 yards and a town renames a bridge". Escalating concrete consequences work when every item is specific.
Lutnick exits: he shipped the machine pick untouched, "back at Cantor by Tuesday, book deal by Thursday, podcast by Lent". A list of consequences that gets pettier as it goes.
